campaign_definition.rule: A military campaign begins when an army's troops leave garrison and ends when they return to garrison.
A short military campaign lasts one month.
Longer campaigns may last seasons or years.

regions.definition: Campaigns occur within regions consisting of several domains or realms.

mapping_requirements.rule: Regions should be mapped beforehand on hex paper.
The regional map should show terrain by hex, major domains, urban settlements, navigable waterways, and roads.
Standard medium region hex paper is 32 small hexes wide by 48 small hexes long, with 24-mile reference hexes superimposed 8 wide by 12 long.
For larger regions, scale upward so each small hex equals 24 miles.

step.name: initiative
step.rule: Each army leader rolls 1d6 and adds strategic ability to determine initiative.
A leader may order a forced march before rolling initiative to gain +2 initiative.
Ties are resolved in favor of the leader with higher strategic ability; if still tied, re-roll.

step.name: movement_and_battles
step.rule: Leaders act from highest initiative downward.
A leader may delay his army's initiative to any lower count down to the negative value of his initiative score.
The army currently taking its turn is the acting army.
The acting army selects offensive, defensive, or evasive strategic stance.
The acting army moves on the regional map.
If movement enters a domain controlled by another leader without permission, the army has invaded the domain.
After movement, the Judge makes a reconnaissance roll for the acting army against nearby opposing armies.
The Judge then makes reconnaissance rolls for each nearby opposing army against the acting army.
If the acting army ends in the same 6-mile hex as another army, a battle may occur.
If one army is in a stronghold, a siege may result.
After all battles or sieges triggered by the acting army are resolved, initiative passes to the next highest leader.

step.name: supply
step.rule: Each army checks whether it is in supply.
If in supply, it pays supply cost.
If not in supply, it resolves the consequences of lacking supplies.

step.name: occupation_and_conquest
step.rule: Resolve the outcomes of invasions.
Successful invaders may occupy, conquer, and/or pillage domains.

entry.rule: Shift the time increment from weeks to days.
Use the same procedure, but resolve movement, battles, invasion, reconnaissance, and related activities daily.
Supply is still checked only once per week.
The Judge may resolve movement and activities more casually without strict weekly procedure.

stance.name: offensive
stance.rule: The army actively seeks battle with opposing armies.

stance.name: defensive
stance.rule: The army fights if battle is offered but does not otherwise attack.

stance.name: evasive
stance.rule: The army avoids battle if possible.

formation_requirements.rule: When choosing a stance, the army must assign one-quarter to one-third of its divisions to the vanguard.
When choosing a stance, the army must assign one-quarter to one-third of its divisions to the rear guard.
All remaining divisions are the main body.
Vanguard divisions lead the marching order and are most likely to fight an offensive battle.
Rear guard divisions protect the flank of an evading army and are most likely to fight an evasive battle.

change_rules.rule: Strategic stance may be changed freely whenever initiative is rolled.
With the Judge's permission, strategic stance may also be changed when a new opposing army is detected.

general_rules.rule: Armies move on the regional map.
Army movement is based on the encounter movement rate of its troops.
Travel rates are based on a full day of movement through open, clear terrain.
An army traveling in formation moves at the speed of its slowest unit.

rest_and_recuperation.rule: Armies moving long distances must rest 3 days out of every 7 to resupply and care for pack animals.
The listed weekly movement rates already include this rest requirement.
If an army marches more than 4 days out of 7 without resting, all units suffer a cumulative -1 penalty to attack throws and damage rolls per extra day until required rest is made up.

entry.name: tireless_troops
entry.rule: Tireless troops do not need rest.
Tireless troops may march every day.
Tireless troops may forced march without penalty.

forced_marching.definition: Forced marching increases travel to 12 hours per day instead of 8.
forced_marching.rule: A leader may order a forced march before initiative is rolled or during his initiative.
If ordered before initiative, the army gains +2 initiative.
If ordered during initiative, no initiative bonus is gained.
Forced marching increases daily movement by 50%.
Each day of forced marching counts as 2 days of marching for rest and recuperation purposes.
The double-counting penalty applies even if the army does not exceed its normal daily movement.

large_armies.definition: Armies occupying 2 or more 6-mile hexes move more slowly because of column length.

rules.rule: Army-size movement multipliers apply in addition to terrain movement multipliers.
If a multi-hex army occupies multiple terrain types, use the worst movement multiplier.
A large army may split into divisions and march separately.
Separated divisions function as separate armies until regrouped by moving back into adjacent hexes.

war_machines.definition: War machines include artillery, battering rams, galleries, hoists, screws, and siege towers.

assembly_rules.rule: Assembling or disassembling a war machine is a construction project.
Construction cost is 1/100 of the cost to build the war machine from scratch.
Minimum assembly or disassembly time is 1 day.
Disassembled war machines cannot be used until assembled.
An army surprised on the march or forced into sudden battle cannot use disassembled artillery or devices.

supply_requirements.rule: An army on campaign must remain in supply at all times.
To be in supply, an army must be able to pay its supply cost.
To be in supply, an army must have supply base value at least equal to supply cost.
To be in supply, an army must have a clear line of supply to its supply base.

base_rules.rule: Weekly supply cost is 60gp per unit of 120 infantry.
Weekly supply cost is 240gp per unit of 60 cavalry.
Other creature types use the Exotic Creatures Roster.
Smaller- or larger-scale units cost proportionately more or less per unit.
Supply cost includes food, water, pack animals, and handlers.
Units without a quartermaster cost double to supply.

entry.name: carnivorous_troops
entry.rule: Carnivorous troops or mounts usually cost 4 times as much to supply.
Battle casualties or captured prisoners may be fed to carnivorous troops.
Each casualty or prisoner provides meat value in gp equal to its base XP value.
If a non-Chaotic unit sees casualties or prisoners of its own race eaten by a carnivorous unit from the same army, that unit suffers a calamity and must make a loyalty roll.

entry.name: hungerless_troops
entry.rule: Hungerless troops have no supply cost.
Hungerless troops do not need to maintain lines of supply.
Hungerless troops are never out of supply.

supply_base.definition: A supply base converts supply cost in gold into food, water, and provisions.
supply_base.rule: Any friendly or occupied city, town, or stronghold can serve as a supply base.
An army may use one or more supply bases.
Total supply base value must equal or exceed the army's supply cost.

value_calculation.rule: Supply base value includes the monthly income after expenses of the base itself.
Supply base value includes the monthly income after expenses of any friendly domains in the same 24-mile hex.
Supply base value includes the value of any supply bases to which it has a clear line of supply.

construction_and_change_rules.rule: An army may construct a small border fort as a 10,000gp construction project.
A constructed border fort functions as a Class VI market for supply purposes.
Armies may construct chains of supply bases to maintain supply from a distant capital.
An army may change supply bases at any time.
A captured stronghold may become a new supply base.

line_of_supply.definition: A line of supply is the route between the army and its supply base, or between supply bases.
line_of_supply.rule: A line of supply is clear only if it is neither blocked nor overextended.

blocked_supply.rule: A supply line is blocked if it passes through any hex occupied by enemy forces.
An army with a blocked supply line is out of supply until the enemy is removed or a new unobstructed route is found.

overextended_supply.rule: A supply line is overextended if its weighted length exceeds 16 hexes, equal to 96 miles.
An army with an overextended line is out of supply until the line is shortened to legal length.

weighted_length_rules.rule: Count each barren or desert hex as 4 hexes.
Count each jungle, mountain, or swamp hex as 2 hexes.
Count every 2 hill or woods hexes as 3 hexes.
Count every 4 road hexes as 1 hex.
Count every 3 settled hexes as 1 hex.
Do not count hexes along a navigable waterway.

racial_modifiers.rule: Elves treat forest terrain as settled for supply-line measurement.
Dwarves treat hills and mountains as settled for supply-line measurement.
Beastmen treat all terrain as settled for supply-line measurement.

requisition_and_looting.definition: An army that is out of supply may take supplies from peasant families in domains it passes through.

requisition_rules.rule: Orderly requisition yields 40gp of supplies per peasant family.
Orderly requisition leaves peasants enough supplies to survive.
Supplies can be requisitioned from a domain only once every 6 months.

looting_rules.rule: Additional supplies beyond requisition must be looted.
Looting yields up to 20gp of supplies per peasant family.
For each 20gp of supplies looted, 1 peasant family is lost.
A domain may be reduced to zero peasant families through requisition plus looting.
The total possible supply extracted is 60gp per family.

operational_rules.rule: The domain's leader may resist requisition or looting by fighting a battle.
A moving army may requisition all of its supplies from one hex or fractionally from each hex traveled through.
Any requisitioning or looting by a moving army halves its movement rate.
An encamped army must requisition first from the hexes it occupies, then from adjacent hexes.

physical_effects.rule: Insufficiently supplied troops lose 1 hit point per day.
Insufficiently supplied troops suffer a cumulative -1 penalty to attack throws and damage rolls.
Insufficiently supplied troops cannot heal naturally.
If troops eat enough food for one day, they regain natural healing, recover 1 hit point lost to hunger, and reduce hunger penalties by 1.
Troops receiving food every other day or half rations daily can function almost indefinitely.

psychological_effects.rule: Each week a unit is partially or completely unsupplied counts as a calamity.
Each such unit must make a loyalty roll.

partial_supply_allocation.rule: If an army can feed only some units, its leader chooses which units are supplied.
Supplied units suffer no lack-of-supply penalties and do not make the weekly lack-of-supply check.
Unsupplied units suffer an additional -1 penalty on their loyalty rolls because they are visibly being left to starve.

simplified_supply.rule: In well-populated areas along roads and waterways, the Judge may simply deduct weekly supply cost from the leader's treasury.
Under the simplified method, check supply only if the army is cut off by enemies, crosses hostile or unsettled terrain, or moves more than 24 miles from a road or waterway.

reconnaissance.definition: Reconnaissance rolls abstract intelligence gathering and counter-intelligence during campaigns.

frequency.rule: After each army completes movement, the Judge makes a reconnaissance roll for that army against any nearby armies in range.
The Judge then makes a reconnaissance roll for each nearby army against the army that just moved.
The number of reconnaissance rolls is not capped; each nearby enemy in range may generate one roll.
Reconnaissance rolls are always made by the Judge in secret.
If bookkeeping is burdensome, multiple friendly armies within one 24-mile hex may be consolidated into one reconnaissance effort.

step.rule: Roll 2d6.
Apply reconnaissance modifiers.
Cross-reference the modified roll on the reconnaissance results table.

entry.name: proximity_of_dispersed_armies
entry.rule: If only the observing army is dispersed, count proximity from its closest unit to the opposing army.
If only the opposing army is dispersed, count proximity from the observing army to the largest opposing division or body of troops.
If both armies are dispersed, count proximity from the closest observing unit to the largest opposing division.

entry.name: magic_scrying
entry.rule: Each crystal ball counts as 1 spell effect.
Every 3 castings of scry count as 1 spell effect.
The spellcaster must know someone in the opposing army or already know the army's location to use scrying.
If an officer is protected by amulet versus crystal balls and ESP or nondetection, that officer and units under his command cannot be scryed upon.
An army is fully protected from scrying only if every officer is protected.
Commune or contact other plane may provide information through question-and-answer mechanics or count as a +1 modifier, at the Judge's discretion.

entry.name: magic_camouflage
entry.rule: Magical camouflage reduces the effective size of the opposing army for observation purposes.
Each hallucinatory terrain, massmorph, or permanent illusion hides 1 company-sized unit.

entry.name: scouting_and_screening_range
entry.rule: Cavalry and flyers on garrison duty scout and screen within the domain they garrison.
Cavalry and flyers in an army on campaign scout and screen only their own 24-mile hex and adjacent 24-mile hexes.
Reconnaissance rolls between armies 3 or more 24-mile hexes apart are not modified by scouting or screening troops.
The scouting and screening table assumes company-sized units.
Treat each battalion-sized unit as 4 units for scouting and screening.
Treat each brigade-sized unit as 16 units for scouting and screening.

entry.name: spies
entry.rule: Infiltrated spies modify reconnaissance rolls as described in the spying hijink rules.

entry.name: stratagems
entry.rule: Reconnaissance stratagem modifiers are assigned by the Judge based on actions by PCs or major NPCs.

entry.name: catastrophe
entry.rule: The observing army receives false intelligence.
The Judge presents the result as if it were a major success.

entry.name: failure
entry.rule: The observing army gains no intelligence.
If the opposing army was previously undetected, the observing army may remain unaware of its existence.

entry.name: marginal_success
entry.rule: The observing army gains limited intelligence based on proximity.

entry.name: success
entry.rule: The observing army gains substantial intelligence based on proximity.

entry.name: major_success
entry.rule: The observing army gains the greatest available intelligence based on proximity.

intelligence_definitions.rule: Location indicates the opposing army's position relative to the observing army, with precision based on result and distance.
Approximate size categories are small (600 or fewer), average (600 to 3,000), large (3,001 to 12,000), huge (12,001 to 36,000), gigantic (36,001 to 72,000), and colossal (72,001 or more).
Number of divisions reveals command organization.
Number of units per division also reveals whether the army uses company-, battalion-, or brigade-sized units.
Type of each unit reveals unit roles such as heavy infantry, light cavalry, or war elephants.
Strength of each unit reveals actual troop counts and understrength units.

acquisition_rules.rule: Prisoners may be deserters, foragers, scouts, or turncoats.
Each prisoner knows 1d3 pieces of information.
For each piece of information, roll 1d4 on the prisoner information table using the appropriate prisoner value column.
If the same information topic is rolled twice, shift one column right on the table to increase detail.
The Judge should make prisoner-information rolls in secret and determine the prisoner's identity accordingly.

interrogation_rules.rule: The Judge may roleplay interrogation and/or roll 2d6 on the interrogation results table.
The roll is modified by the interrogator's Charisma, applicable proficiencies such as Bribery, Diplomacy, Intimidation, or Seduction, and other reasonable factors.
On 2 or less, the prisoner gives 1 piece of false information and the Judge presents it as if it were true.
On 3-5, the prisoner reveals nothing of value.
On 6-8, the prisoner reveals 1 piece of information.
On 9-11, the prisoner reveals 2 pieces of information.
On 12 or more, the prisoner reveals all known information.
Without magic, there is no way to know for sure how many pieces of information a prisoner has or whether it is true.
Magic such as charm or ESP may be used to extract or verify information.

stratagems.definition: Stratagems are special operations to reconnoiter, scout, slay enemy scouts, deceive enemy scouts, or otherwise influence campaign intelligence.
stratagems.rule: For NPC stratagems, the Judge may assign a modifier from +1 to +3 to a friendly reconnaissance roll or -1 to -3 to an enemy roll.
If PCs carry out the stratagem personally, the Judge may resolve it using Heroic Forays rules.
Each 1/2 point of BR at stake in a Heroic Foray stratagem grants +1 to the army's reconnaissance roll.

access_requirement.rule: Once an opposing army has been located, a leader with access to a syndicate or other source of perpetrators may order hijinks against it.
Before any hijink other than spying can be performed, a perpetrator must be infiltrated into the enemy army as a spy.

hijink.name: spying
hijink.rule: A successful spying hijink infiltrates a perpetrator into the opposing army.
The perpetrator must succeed on Hide in Shadows.
The perpetrator must be of the same race as the opposing army or also succeed on a Disguise proficiency throw.
The perpetrator must speak the language of the opposing army.
Each infiltrated perpetrator grants +1 on reconnaissance rolls made against the opposing army during the next month.
During that month, the infiltrated perpetrator may attempt assassination, carousing, disinformation, sabotage, or stealing.
At the end of the month, another spying hijink is required to remain infiltrated.
If caught, the charge is treason.

hijink.name: assassination
hijink.rule: An infiltrated perpetrator may target an identified enemy officer.
The perpetrator must succeed on Hide in Shadows.
Apply a -1 penalty per level the perpetrator is lower than the victim.
Further modify the throw by the target officer's morale modifier.
If caught, the charge is murder.

hijink.name: carousing
hijink.rule: An infiltrated perpetrator may gather information through carousing.
The perpetrator must succeed on Hear Noise.
Success grants 1 piece of common information, as if interrogating a prisoner.
Valuable information may be sought at -2 on the throw.
Very valuable information may be sought at -5 on the throw.
If caught, the charge is sedition.

hijink.name: disinformation
hijink.rule: An infiltrated perpetrator may spread lies and rumors through carousing.
The perpetrator must succeed on Hear Noise.
Success imposes a -2 penalty on the opposing army's reconnaissance rolls for the next month.
If caught, the charge is sedition.

hijink.name: sabotage
hijink.rule: An infiltrated perpetrator may attempt to destroy enemy supplies.
The perpetrator must succeed on Move Silently.
Modify the throw by the opposing leader's strategic ability.
Success destroys 1,000gp of supplies per class level.
The perpetrator may attempt to destroy additional supplies by taking -1 on the throw per extra 1,000gp.
If caught, the charge is arson.

hijink.name: stealing
hijink.rule: An infiltrated perpetrator may attempt to steal the flag of an enemy unit.
The perpetrator must succeed on Pick Pockets.
Modify the throw by the target unit's morale score.
If successful, the target unit immediately makes a loyalty roll at -1 because it has lost its flag.
Stealing the army's main emblem imposes a -10 penalty on the throw.
If the army emblem is stolen, each unit in the army makes a loyalty roll at -1.
If caught, the charge is sedition.

risks_of_hijinks.rule: Hijinks against armies are highly risky.
If caught, severe charges are levied and neither attorneys nor interpleaders are available.
If convicted, the perpetrator suffers normal punishment and is also interrogated as a prisoner.
A 0th-4th level perpetrator counts as a common prisoner.
A 5th-9th level perpetrator counts as a valuable prisoner.
A 10th level or higher perpetrator counts as a very valuable prisoner.
If the perpetrator is a PC, the Judge may allow negotiation of a reduced sentence in exchange for information.

invasion.rule: If an army enters a domain controlled by another leader without permission, it has invaded the domain.
An invaded domain immediately makes a domain morale roll.
Only garrison forces physically present in the domain count for that morale determination.
If the domain's own garrison is away campaigning, morale suffers from its absence.
A friendly army from the same realm present in the domain counts as a garrison even if not directly controlled by the domain ruler.

occupation.definition: A domain is occupied when invading troops are numerous enough to constitute an effective garrison.
occupation.rule: Calculate the wages per month of occupying troops in the domain.
Subtract the wages per month of the owner's troops still in the domain after battles.
Divide the difference by the number of peasant families.
If the resulting gp value of occupying troops per peasant exceeds the domain's garrison cost, the domain is occupied.

effects_of_occupation.rule: Control of the domain's families and revenues passes to the occupier.
Responsibility for garrisoning the domain passes to the occupier.
Responsibility for holding festivals passes to the occupier.
Responsibility for paying taxes and tithes passes to the occupier.
Taxes paid during occupation go to the occupier's lord, not the owner's lord.

morale_during_occupation.rule: While a domain is occupied but not conquered, track separate domain morale scores for the owner and the occupier.
The occupier's initial domain morale score is 0 minus the owner's domain morale.
Each season after occupation begins, make 2 domain morale rolls: one for the owner and one for the occupier.
Apply separate adjustments based on alignment, garrison strength, and other factors for each leader.
If the domain becomes Turbulent, Defiant, or Rebellious toward the occupier, peasants fight to restore the rightful leader.
If the domain becomes Turbulent, Defiant, or Rebellious toward the owner, peasants become insurgents rooting out loyalists.

conquest.definition: A domain is conquered when all strongholds and settlements within it have been captured.
conquest.rule: A stronghold or settlement is captured when no opposing units are present within it.
Ungarrisoned strongholds or urban settlements may be captured automatically.
Garrisoned strongholds or settlements must be besieged.

post_conquest_options.rule: A conqueror may assimilate the new domain into his personal domain only if it is adjacent and his personal domain is not at maximum size.
If not eligible or desired for direct assimilation, the domain may be added to the conqueror's realm under a vassal or sub-vassal.
A conquered domain may also be pillaged.

pillaging.definition: Pillaging is looting and devastation of a conquered domain instead of integrating it into the realm.
pillaging.rule: Pillaging requires a sizable force and time based on domain size.
Prisoners taken from pillage may be kept as slaves or ransomed or sold for 40gp each.
Pillaging reduces domain population and reduces stronghold value or urban investment.

procedural_rules.rule: If remaining stronghold value or urban investment after pillaging cannot sustain the remaining population, excess population is lost when pillaging ends.
A pillaged domain immediately makes a domain morale roll at -4.
A domain may be pillaged repeatedly; each pillage uses the domain's current size.

entry.name: salting_the_earth
entry.rule: Destroying a domain completely takes 4 times the normal pillaging time.
Salting the earth yields 20gp in plunder per family.
Salting the earth yields 50gp in supplies per family.
Salting the earth yields 1 prisoner per family.
The domain is destroyed and cannot be looted further.

entry.name: pillaging_with_too_small_a_force
entry.rule: An undersized army may still pillage.
Roll pillage results normally, then multiply gold, supplies, and prisoners by the ratio of troops available to troops required.
Time required is unchanged.

entry.name: interrupted_pillaging
entry.rule: An army pillaging a domain may not move.
An enemy army may attack the pillaging army.
If pillaging is interrupted before completion, roll results normally and multiply gold, supplies, and prisoners by the ratio of time spent pillaging to time required.
If the force is both undersized and interrupted, apply both reductions proportionately.

experience_rule.rule: Gold earned from pillaging counts as spoils of war for experience purposes.

domain_size_handling.rule: If one hex contains a mix of domains and Class V or Class VI urban settlements, sum the families and treat them as a single domain for invasion, occupation, conquest, and pillage.
Urban settlements of Class IV or higher are treated as separate domains for invasion, occupation, conquest, and pillage.

pillaging_supply_bases.rule: If the pillaged domain or settlement is serving as a supply base, add extra gold equal to 1 month's wages for the opposing army.
If the pillaged domain or settlement is serving as a supply base, add extra supplies equal to 1 month's supply cost for the opposing army.
These rules assume wages and supplies are cached at the supply base in advance and moved forward when needed.
The Judge may adjust the result if the actual situation differs from that assumption.
When an army's supply base is pillaged, its wages and supply costs are doubled for the next month.
The sack of a supply base counts as a calamity for morale purposes.
